rv.q: The production ultimately feels as flat as a fallen house of cards.
Howard and Winger have real chemistry, a push-pull dynamic that runs the gamut from flirtatious to downright nasty.
It does provide the opportunity for this indelible experience of watching two terrific, well-known actors performing their hearts out practically within arm’s reach.
Yet in its latest incarnation, at Soho’s Housing Works Bookstore, this vehicle, like its characters, shows marked signs of rust.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this revival of Coburn's Pulitzer winner, with critics divided on whether the aging play still resonates. Strong performances earn praise, but some find the drama emotionally hollow and tedious.

vr.q: even with my reservations, it's hard not to recommend taking the opportunity to see this classic play performed by these actors at this price point and this level of intimacy
